context.text: This is the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Mike Rounds, who first took office in 2015. Rounds defeated Justin McNeal 75.8%-24.2% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. South Dakota's Democratic primary was canceled after Julian Beaudion ran unopposed for the nomination, but Beaudion subsequently withdrew or was disqualified before the general election; Brian Bengs, the 2022 Democratic Senate nominee, is running against Rounds in the general election as an independent.

summary.text: Mike Rounds is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to the U.S. Senate. He previously served as Governor of South Dakota (2003-2011) and in the South Dakota Senate, including as majority leader.

background.text: Born in Huron, South Dakota, in 1954; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from South Dakota State University (1977). Worked as an insurance executive.
Served in the South Dakota Senate from 1991 to 2000, including as minority whip (1993-1994) and majority leader (1995-2000).
Served as Governor of South Dakota from 2003 to 2011.

positions.summary: Sponsored S. 4880, the Dismemberment Abortion Ban Act of 2026, a bill to prohibit dismemberment abortions.
Cosponsored S. 65, the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2025, a bill to allow reciprocity for the carrying of certain concealed firearms.

Cosponsored S. 9, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, which provides that for Title IX compliance in athletics, sex is recognized based solely on reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
Cosponsored S. 128, the SAVE Act, a bill to amend the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, chairs the Armed Services Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and the Banking Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment, and also serves on the Senate Committee on Appropriations, the Committee on Indian Affairs and the Select Committee on Intelligence.

summary.text: Brian Bengs, the 2022 Democratic nominee for this seat, is running as an independent against Mike Rounds. He is a U.S. Air Force veteran, attorney and former university professor who campaigns on getting money out of politics and lowering the cost of living.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Air Force.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history and international studies from Iowa State University (1994), a J.D. from the University of Iowa (1996), a master's degree in history from Louisiana Tech University (2007), and a master's degree in international and comparative law from George Washington University (2007).
Worked as an assistant professor at Northern State University and as chief of general law/assistant general counsel for the U.S. Air Force.
Was the Democratic nominee for this same U.S. Senate seat in 2022, losing to John Thune 69.6%-26.1%.

priorities.text: Getting money out of politics, saying "Big Money" has corrupted the political system so regular people cannot afford the lifestyle their parents had.
Balancing the federal budget and paying down the national debt.
Making daily life more affordable, including establishing affordable and accessible healthcare and safeguarding Social Security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Lists establishing affordable and accessible healthcare among his priorities, alongside safeguarding Social Security and Medicare.
